title: Resampling-free jitter-aware bundle adjustment for HiRISE multi-CCD stereo mapping on Mars
venue: ISPRS Journal of Photogrammetry and Remote Sensing
abstract: Accurate topographic reconstruction from High Resolution Imaging Science Experiment (HiRISE) stereo imagery is essential for Martian geomorphological analysis and landing-site assessment. However, high-frequency sensor jitter and geometric inconsistency among non-collinear charge-coupled devices (CCDs) can introduce seam-related artifacts, periodic residuals, and local digital elevation model (DEM) deformation. Conventional correction workflows often estimate jitter in image space or update attitude parameters before stereo measurement, and therefore do not fully exploit the internal overlap constraints of the HiRISE focal plane within bundle adjustment. This paper presents a resampling-free photogrammetric framework for HiRISE multi-CCD stereo mapping, in which harmonic jitter compensation is embedded directly into rigorous bundle adjustment. A time-continuous exterior orientation model combines low-order polynomial motion with Fourier-series-based jitter terms initialized from adjacent-CCD overlap disparities. Inter-orbit stereo tie points and inter-CCD overlap tie points are then jointly used to constrain stereo geometry, time-dependent pointing variation, and focal-plane consistency in a unified adjustment model. For original CCD-image matching, a constrained coarse-to-fine pipeline is developed. Pretrained XFeat with test-time descriptor adaptation is used mainly for prior-free coarse initialization at the lowest pyramid level, and the resulting geometric relation is propagated to guide efficient Harris + normalized cross-correlation (NCC) refinement and dense grid matching under local constraints. Experiments on four HiRISE stereo pairs covering the Spirit landing region, Mawrth Vallis, the Zhurong landing region, and a more topographically challenging inverted-channel area in Gale Crater are used to evaluate the proposed framework under different terrain-relief conditions. The results show that the proposed framework maintains sub-pixel mean check-point reprojection residuals in both image directions across all four stereo pairs, suppresses jitter-induced periodic residuals, improves consistency across CCD seams, and produces DEMs consistent with the Mars Orbiter Laser Altimeter (MOLA) and official HiRISE/Planetary Data System (PDS) references without image resampling. The implementation will be made publicly available at: https://github.com/wbl1997/mars_images_ba.git .

title: Enhanced early warning of extreme river discharge events in the Yangtze River Basin using atmospheric circulation signals
venue: International Journal of Applied Earth Observation and Geoinformation
abstract: Early warning of extreme river discharge events (ERDEs) is crucial for water resources management and disaster reduction in the Yangtze River Basin (YRB), yet substantial uncertainty remains in their prediction. This study proposes a novel strategy to enhance ERDE early warning by detecting its associated atmospheric circulation signals. We develop DetRF, a machine learning model that integrates anomaly detection with a balanced random forest ensemble. DetRF was trained and validated using ERA5 reanalysis data from 2000 to 2019 and independently applied to 2020–2024, with its early warning performance evaluated against satellite-based precipitation and reanalysis river discharge data. Across eight subregions of the YRB, DetRF effectively detects ERDE-related atmospheric circulation signals, achieving mean recall, precision, and F1 score values of 0.756, 0.506, and 0.576, respectively, and consistently outperforming benchmark machine learning models. The detected signals accurately capture key synoptic features associated with hydrological extremes, including the positions and intensities of troughs, vortices, and cyclones, as well as moisture transport. More than 99% of the detected signals are followed by precipitation within five days, while persistent precipitation occurs in over 67% of cases across both local and upstream regions. More importantly, an average of 93.8% of DetRF-detected circulation signals are followed by at least one ERDE within the subsequent five days. These findings establish a direct link between specific atmospheric circulation signals and subsequent hydrological extremes, offering a new pathway for extending ERDE early warning beyond conventional hydrological prediction. The proposed framework is particularly promising for regions where hydrological observations are sparse.

title: Estimating supraglacial lake bottom ablation rates by integrating ICESat-2 repeat track data and multi-temporal sentinel-2 imagery
venue: International Journal of Applied Earth Observation and Geoinformation
abstract: Supraglacial lakes are widely distributed across the Greenland Ice Sheet (GrIS) each summer. The resulting meltwater-enhanced ablation effect plays a critical role in understanding the GrIS surface mass balance but remains poorly quantified. Inspired by the insight that longer meltwater persistence leads to stronger meltwater-enhanced ablation, this study proposes a novel method to directly estimate supraglacial lake bottom ablation rates at centimeter-per-day scale using satellite observations. First, we map multi-temporal supraglacial lake extents from Sentinel-2 imagery to estimate cumulative meltwater-covered days. Then, we derive ablation depths at the lake bottom and surrounding bare ice by differencing ICESat-2 repeat track data acquired before and during the melt season. Next, we perform linear fitting between lake bottom ablation depths and cumulative meltwater-covered days along the ICESat-2 tracks to calculate both the lake bottom ablation rate and the bare ice ablation rate. Finally, we evaluate the magnitude of the meltwater-enhanced ablation effect. We apply this method to 26 supraglacial lakes across the GrIS and identify a positive linear relationship between lake bottom ablation depths and cumulative water-covered days (mean Pearson correlation coefficient r = 0.70 ± 0.14, p < 0.001). The fitted mean lake bottom ablation rate (4.50 ± 1.15 cm/day) significantly exceeds the mean bare ice ablation rate (1.98 ± 0.52 cm/day). Meltwater in supraglacial lakes therefore enhances ablation rate by ∼ 1.3 ± 0.5 times, with values ranging from 0.6 to 2.4, consistent with previous field measurements (1.1–1.4 times) and numerical model simulations (1.1–1.7 times). In summary, this study provides a first quantitative satellite-based estimate of meltwater-enhanced ablation across the GrIS under varying ablation intensities, and may improve our understanding of GrIS surface melt process.

title: Analysis of intraday urban thermal anisotropy and downward shortwave radiation through UAV experiment and coupled model
venue: International Journal of Applied Earth Observation and Geoinformation
abstract: The pronounced thermal radiation anisotropy observed in rapidly urbanizing areas arises from the complex interplay of solar downward shortwave radiation (DSWR), building geometry, and local topography. To address this, we propose a novel framework, termed GRay-AU3SM-IRT, for the analysis of urban thermal anisotropy (UTA). The study was conducted in a representative mountainous city in Chongqing, China. A specific 0.4 × 0.4 km 2 area, characterized by buildings and terrain on 10° slopes, was selected for analysis at hourly resolution. The simulations showed strong agreement with measured data, achieving a root mean square error below 0.46 K and a coefficient of determination exceeding 0.79. The analysis reveals that UTA shows pronounced diurnal variations: it intensifies gradually in the morning, peaks at solar noon with clear hotspot formation, and generates secondary hotspots in the afternoon due to changing solar azimuth and slope effects. The morning striped distribution pattern caused by building geometry diminishes with declining solar irradiance and disappears by afternoon. Diurnal trends in the UTA Effect (UTAE), directional brightness temperature (DBT), DBT Effect (DBTE), and DSWR are generally aligned. Notably, UTAE and DBTE peak before DSWR, while both maximum and minimum DBT peak later. The proposed framework offers key advantages: precise multi-lap UAV navigation, minimized motion artifacts, consistent temporal sampling via adaptive velocity control, gap-filling through simulation, and spatio-temporal outlier correction. It provides critical data for angle normalization and correction across diverse urban environments.

title: Remote-sensing-assisted and in situ-constrained reconstruction of 4-hourly chlorophyll-a dynamics in inland lakes using vision Mamba and temporal attention
venue: International Journal of Applied Earth Observation and Geoinformation
abstract: Chlorophyll a (Chl-a) is widely used to indicate eutrophication and bloom risk in inland waters, but daily Sentinel-3 observations alone cannot resolve transient sub-daily variability represented in partially observed 4-hourly in situ Chl-a records. This study therefore develops VGTA (Vision Mamba–GKOA–TCN-Attention), a staged remote-sensing-assisted and in situ-constrained framework that integrates daily Sentinel-3 OLCI-derived priors with partially observed 4-hourly in situ Chl-a sequences and binary observation masks. A 20-dimensional OLCI-derived feature space provides spectral–spatial priors for Chl-a estimation and bloom-risk state identification. GKOA optimizes TCN-Attention to reconstruct masked values within partially observed 4-hourly in situ Chl-a sequences. Vision Mamba outperformed CNN– and Transformer-based models in Chl-a estimation, achieving 94.8% accuracy, a Macro-F1 score of 0.909, and a Bloom-F1 score of 0.870. Ablation experiments confirmed the contributions of bidirectional contextual modeling, positional embedding, selective state-space modeling, and gating. Under Missing Completely at Random, block-missing, and real missing scenarios, GTA improved reconstruction performance by 12.71–55.54% relative to the best baseline models. Uncertainty increased once continuous gaps reached seven days, defining a practical boundary of data-driven reconstruction. Chl-a fluctuations and bloom-risk transitions can unfold within a day, and daily satellite snapshots may blur their timing or miss short events. Reconstruction of masked time steps within partially observed 4-hourly in situ Chl-a sequences can support earlier identification of bloom-risk transitions, more timely field sampling and management responses, and temporally finer monitoring of inland waters.

title: Reference-anchored envelope modelling for predicting tree mortality hotspots driven by drought
venue: International Journal of Applied Earth Observation and Geoinformation
abstract: Predicting tree mortality hotspots driven by drought remains challenging, since vulnerability to drought is strongly influenced by climate, landform, and substrate. We propose a novel reference-anchored, quantile-envelope susceptibility model-implemented through a reproducible workflow- that exports mortality-resemblance (high-risk) environments from three confirmed tree-mortality footprints (training AOIs), based on semi-arid conifer and evergreen sclerophyllous forests in Cyprus, to produce wide screening layers. The approach combines (i) physiographic similarity derived from AOI-calibrated envelopes for slope, multi-scale topographic position and curvature (broad quantiles; majority-rule), (ii) exposure constraints via circular aspect windows, warm-season solar loading (April-September) and substrate (lithology) filtering, (iii) a drought severity gate (SPEI-12 (Standardized Precipitation-Evapotranspiration Index-12) ≤ -1.4), and (iv) Landsat event-year spectral collapse relative to a fixed 3-year pre-event baseline, coupled with a year + 1 persistence rule to suppress transient stress. Our within-AOI evaluation (forest-only) showed substantial representativeness (coverage 70.49–85.35%), while recovering most reference mortality pixels (recall 67.62–100%). In 2025, two independent mortality sites were identified in Cyprus, coinciding with exceptional drought (SPEI < -2) and a sharp decline in the Normalized Burn Ratio (NBR) consistent with foliage browning, and occurring within high-risk zones as mapped in the final risk map. As a plausibility check, both 2025 sites fell within pre-mapped high-risk zones, with 83.50% and 82.69% of their forested area exceeding HEAT ≥ 0.60 and mean risk scores of 84.91% and 75.55%, respectively. With 18.88% of Cyprus’s total forest flagged as high-risk, the probability of this co-occurrence being random is p ≈ 0.036 (binomial test). Anchoring calibration to local mortality footprints makes the approach readily transferable to other regions with documented events.

title: A Targeted–Refined Framework for wind turbine detection integrating AlphaEarth Foundations and high-resolution multispectral satellite imagery
venue: International Journal of Applied Earth Observation and Geoinformation
abstract: The rapid expansion of clean energy systems, particularly wind and solar power, has made large-scale monitoring of related infrastructure using high-resolution multispectral satellite imagery increasingly important yet challenging. Conventional wind turbine detection approaches rely on pixel-level analysis of high-resolution imagery or sliding-window strategies. These methods often suffer from computational redundancy, low efficiency, and false-positive accumulation, making them inadequate for large-area surveys and operational monitoring. To address these limitations, this study proposes a Targeted–Refined Framework that integrates AlphaEarth Foundations (AEF) with high-resolution Jilin-1 imagery. In the Targeted Spatial-Prior Generation Stage, the Unified Spatial Prior Generation Framework (USPGF) is developed to generate high-recall wind turbine candidate regions from AEF land-surface semantic embeddings, thereby replacing exhaustive full-area search with targeted candidate screening. In the Refined Detection Stage, the candidate regions are spatially matched to the corresponding high-resolution Jilin-1 image tiles, which are then processed using a YOLO-based model for refined wind turbine localization. Experimental results showed that fewer than 5 % of the high-resolution image tiles were retained by the Targeted Spatial-Prior Generation Stage, and the proposed framework achieved a recall of 96.85 %, a precision of 98.41 %, and an F1-score of 97.63 % on the Tianjin test set. Furthermore, the proposed Targeted–Refined Framework was directly applied to the Beijing–Hebei (BH) region for cross-regional evaluation. In this evaluation, the framework produced 1,580 detections, including 1,512 true positives and 68 false positives, and achieved an F1-score of 91.39 %, indicating favorable cross-regional generalization performance. Overall, this framework provides an efficient and scalable solution for large-scale detection of spatially sparse objects and offers a practical approach for infrastructure inventory and monitoring of wind farms and similar assets.

title: Multi-angular assessment of early-season defoliation: Evaluating the sensitivity of vegetation indices to NPV visibility in temperate broadleaved forests
venue: International Journal of Applied Earth Observation and Geoinformation
abstract: Early-season forest decline in temperate broadleaved stands often lacks detectable biochemical stress signals, manifesting primarily through reduced foliage density and increased visibility of non-photosynthetic vegetation (NPV). This study investigated the spectral separability of green leaves and NPV components under varying levels of canopy defoliation. Using a crane platform, we collected in situ leaf- and canopy-level spectrometer measurements alongside co-aligned photography to quantify the visible fraction of NPV. We analyzed the multi-angular reflectance characteristics and evaluated 35 vegetation indices (VIs) —including green biomass metrics and specialized NPV indices —using Random Forest to identify optimal spectral and geometric configurations. Sunlit young foliage exhibited high forward scatter, creating a nadir reflectance minimum. At canopy level, a nadir minimum was driven by the gap distribution resulting from sustainable forest management practices. Consequently, the optimal viewing angle for top-ranking VIs (e.g., SNC BAO , Ctr 2 , mNDVI 705 ) was near the hotspot geometry, minimizing shadowing and forest floor interference. While the total visible fraction of NPV remained mostly insensitive to viewing angles, its shaded proportion varied. VIs targeting green vegetation via red-edge and NIR domains consistently outperformed dedicated NPV indices based on SWIR cellulose and lignin absorption. This is attributed to low upper-canopy SWIR transmittance, which obscured the signals of the largely shaded NPV fraction. Top-performing VIs achieved R 2 = 0.92 for NPV visibility prediction, improving by 21 % over the best SWIR indices and 11 % over the nadir view. To accurately detect initial defoliation and overcome forest floor interference, adopting off-nadir viewing geometries is advantageous for capturing the optimal signal.

title: Unsupervised soft-min fusion of multi-sensor turbidity products using Gaussian mixture models
venue: International Journal of Applied Earth Observation and Geoinformation
abstract: Turbidity is a key indicator of water quality and particulate dynamics, making its accurate monitoring essential for aquatic ecosystem management. While satellite remote sensing enables large-scale turbidity observation, products derived from different sensors often exhibit inconsistencies due to differences in spectral responses, residual atmospheric effects, and viewing geometries. Effectively integrating such multi-source data in the absence of ground truth remains a significant challenge. Here, we propose Gaussian mixture model-based soft-min (GMMS), a fully unsupervised fusion framework in which neither model construction nor weight estimation relies on ground-truth turbidity observations. GMMS integrates Gaussian mixture modeling with a soft-min weighting strategy to identify latent error-structure contexts and adaptively assign sensor weights according to relative residual stability. By exploiting inter-sensor error characteristics, the framework enables context-aware data fusion. At the overall scale, GMMS significantly outperforms triple collocation (TC) and extended triple collocation for maximized correlation (ETCC) ( p < 0.05). Compared with in situ turbidity observations, GMMS increases the correlation coefficient from 0.798 to 0.841 and reduces the RMSE from 16.849 to 15.921 TU. Site-level evaluations further indicate enhanced robustness and reduced performance variability across monitoring stations. Simulation experiments confirm that GMMS achieves the greatest and most stable performance gains under conditions of moderate-to-high error-structure separability. Overall, GMMS provides an interpretable and transferable unsupervised fusion framework for improving multi-source satellite-derived turbidity estimates in complex riverine environments.

title: GarmentX: Autoregressive parametric representations for 3D garment generation
abstract: This work presents GarmentX, a novel framework for generating diverse, high-fidelity, and wearable 3D garments from a single input image. Traditional methods directly predict 2D pattern edges and their connectivity, an overly unconstrained approach that often leads to severe self-intersections and physically implausible garment structures. In contrast, GarmentX introduces a structured parametric representation compatible with GarmentCode, ensuring that the decoded sewing patterns always form valid, simulation-ready 3D garments while allowing for intuitive modifications of garment shape and style. To achieve this, we employ a masked autoregressive model that sequentially predicts garment parameters, leveraging autoregressive modeling for structured generation while mitigating inconsistencies in direct pattern prediction. Additionally, we introduce GarmentX dataset, containing 378,682 garment parameter–image pairs, constructed through an automatic data generation pipeline that synthesizes diverse garment images conditioned on parametric garment representations. Through integrating our method with GarmentX dataset, we achieve state-of-the-art performance in geometric fidelity and input image alignment, with 100% simulation success that generalizes across diverse body shapes and poses. The complete source code, pre-trained model weights, and the dataset will be released upon publication.

title: Progressive sketch completion meets sketch-modulated diffusion for ancient mural restoration
abstract: Ancient murals often suffer from severe structural damage, where sketches — critical for guiding restoration — are fragmented or entirely missing. Existing edge-guided restoration methods typically assume complete sketches, making them ineffective under realistic deterioration, while current mask generation strategies fail to capture the irregular nature of mural damage. To address these challenges, we propose MuralPaint, a two-stage mural restoration framework that integrates progressive sketch completion with sketch-modulated diffusion. In the first stage, a progressive sketch completion network recovers missing structural information through a coarse-to-fine inference strategy, including coarse reconstruction, local refinement, and global optimization, enabling robust reconstruction of severely broken sketches. In the second stage, we introduce a sketch-modulated diffusion model that integrates the completed sketches into the diffusion process via multi-scale intermediate-feature modulation, enhancing structural fidelity and restoration consistency. In addition, we design a parameterizable damage mask generation algorithm that simulates realistic mural deterioration patterns, including spots, cracks, and peeling. Extensive experiments on both simulated and real-world murals demonstrate that, compared with edge-guided restoration methods and diffusion-based models, MuralPaint more effectively completes damaged sketches and produces visually plausible restorations with coherent structures, showing clear advantages on both simulated and real-world mural restoration tasks. We release the source code at .

title: Pose2Point: Bridging human poses and point clouds for unified action recognition
LR-SMAN: Low-Rank Symmetrical Mutual Attention Network for multispectral object detection
abstract: Multispectral object detection, especially via fusing RGB and infrared (IR) imagery, has attracted growing attention due to its robustness under challenging conditions such as low illumination, nighttime, and adverse weather. Nevertheless, effectively integrating these heterogeneous modalities remains challenging. Existing attention-based fusion methods often adopt asymmetric cross-attention designs and learn cross-modal affinities in a purely data-driven manner without explicit structural constraints, which may yield suboptimal fusion, particularly in complex scenes. To address these issues, we propose a Low-Rank Symmetrical Mutual Attention Network (LR-SMAN) for multispectral object detection. The core of LR-SMAN is twofold: (i) a Symmetrical Mutual Attention (SMA) mechanism that constructs a shared consensus topology and enables balanced, bidirectional cross-modal interactions; and (ii) Tensor Nuclear Norm Regularization (TNNR) imposed on the paired modality-specific affinity tensor to explicitly promote low-rank structure. The proposed regularization suppresses noise and redundancy, encouraging compact, robust, and discriminative shared semantic representations. Extensive experiments show that LR-SMAN achieves competitive performance on several widely used multispectral benchmarks, including VEDAI, M 3 FD, and LLVIP, with particularly notable improvements in challenging settings involving low illumination, small objects, and cluttered backgrounds.

title: Multi-View tensor factorization for dynamic attributed graph embedding with graph-aware features
abstract: Learning node representations in dynamic graphs has garnered significant attention in recent years. However, existing methods face challenges in effectively integrating topology and node attributes within individual snapshots while simultaneously capturing the evolution of graph structure and attributes across snapshots. Motivated by the above challenges, we formulate unsupervised dynamic attributed graph embedding as a coupled multi-view tensor learning problem, where topology, attributes, and graph-aware contextual features are jointly modeled by Multi-View Tensor Factorization (MV-TF) within a shared latent space. The framework explicitly models the coupling between views and incorporates a sparse subspace constraint to enhance embedding quality. Extensive experimental results on node classification tasks demonstrate that our method outperforms state-of-the-art approaches. These results highlight its ability to effectively mine the evolution patterns of dynamic graphs and provide valuable insights for related analyses.

title: SALiT: A structure-aware lightweight Transformer for multi-task remote sensing interpretation
Bias-variance trade-off in radiative transfer model inversion drives uncertainty in leaf area index estimation
abstract: Large-scale leaf area index (LAI) retrieval from satellite observations primarily relies on inverting canopy radiative transfer models (RTMs). Despite the widespread use of various inversion methods, how and why LAI retrievals vary with the method choice remains unclear. Here, within a unified Bayesian framework, we primarily characterized four representative methods as statistical point estimators: (i) numerical optimization (OPT) method; (ii) look-up table (LUT) method; (iii) LUT method with solution averaging (LUT-mean); and (iv) neural network (NN)-based method. Differences in their statistical principles lead to distinct bias-variance trade-offs, causing LAI retrieval RMSEs to vary by 30%–35% across simulated and in situ datasets. Our findings are: (1) The OPT and LUT methods approximate the maximum a posteriori estimator, exhibiting low bias but high variance and producing funnel-shaped scatter between retrieved and reference LAIs. (2) The LUT-mean and NN-based methods reduce variance by introducing bias, leading to overestimation in the mid-LAI range and underestimation in the high-LAI range, thereby producing S-shaped scatter. These characteristics enable the LUT-mean and NN-based methods to achieve lower RMSEs, with the NN-based method approximating the posterior mean estimator and attaining the lowest RMSE. Two alternative machine learning (ML)-based methods, i.e. , random forest (RF) and Gaussian process regression (GPR), share the same statistical interpretation as the NN-based method and exhibit similar retrieval performance. Our study identifies the bias-variance trade-off of inversion methods as one important yet previously underappreciated component of uncertainty in LAI monitoring and highlights the need to consider it in future LAI product development and evaluation.

title: Optically consistent multi-parameter aerosol retrieval from dual-satellite polarimetric observations enabled by physics-guided deep learning
Expert knowledge-guided decision calibration for accurate fine-grained tree species classification
venue: ISPRS Journal of Photogrammetry and Remote Sensing
abstract: Accurate fine-grained tree species classification is critical for forest inventory and biodiversity monitoring. Existing methods predominantly focus on designing complex architectures to fit local data distributions. However, they often overlook the long-tailed distributions and high inter-class similarity inherent in limited data, thereby struggling to distinguish between few-shot or confusing categories. In the process of knowledge dissemination in the human world, individuals will actively seek expert assistance to transcend the limitations of local thinking. Inspired by this, we introduce an external ”Domain Expert” and propose an Expert Knowledge-Guided Classification Decision Calibration Network (EKDC-Net) to overcome these challenges. Our framework addresses two core issues: expert knowledge extraction and utilization. Specifically, we first develop a Local Prior Guided Knowledge Extraction Module (LPKEM). By leveraging Class Activation Map (CAM) analysis, LPKEM guides the domain expert to focus exclusively on discriminative features essential for classification. Subsequently, to effectively integrate this knowledge, we design an Uncertainty-Guided Decision Calibration Module (UDCM). This module dynamically corrects the local model’s decisions by considering both overall category uncertainty and instance-level prediction uncertainty. Furthermore, we present a large-scale classification dataset covering 102 tree species, named CU-Tree102 to address the issue of scarce diversity in current benchmarks. Experiments on three benchmark datasets demonstrate that our approach achieves state-of-the-art performance. Crucially, as a lightweight plug-and-play module, EKDC-Net improves backbone accuracy by 7.86% and precision by 12.89% using only 0.08M additional learnable parameters. The dataset, code, and pre-trained models are available at https://github.com/WHU-USI3DV/TreeCLS .

title: Kinematic pattern interpretation of railway-corridor deformation from InSAR time series with transfer learning-based TCN
venue: International Journal of Applied Earth Observation and Geoinformation
abstract: Railway-corridor deformation monitoring requires timely identification of localized displacement anomalies and characterization of their temporal evolution. Time-series Interferometric Synthetic Aperture Radar (InSAR) provides spatially dense and high-precision displacement observations from repeated SAR acquisitions, but InSAR-based railway studies have largely remained rate-centered, leaving the kinematic information embedded in displacement time series insufficiently exploited. This study develops a kinematic interpretation framework that integrates InSAR displacement time series, transfer learning-based Temporal Convolutional Network (TCN) classification, and multi-source environmental data to characterize railway-corridor deformation in terms of its occurrence, temporal evolution, and environmental context. Sentinel-1 images acquired from January 2022 to December 2024 were processed to retrieve LOS displacement rates and displacement time series along the Kunming–Yuxi section of the China–Laos Railway. To reduce dependence on labeled InSAR samples, a transfer learning strategy was adopted, in which the TCN was pre-trained using simulated displacement sequences and fine-tuned with labeled InSAR observations to classify six kinematic patterns: stable, linear, step, piecewise linear, power-law, and undefined. The corridor is generally stable, with a mean displacement rate of −0.26 mm/year and stable points accounting for 77.96% of observations. Linear and step patterns account for 12.66% and 7.87%, respectively. Strong subsidence zones, where the localized displacement rate reaches −28.43 mm/year, are dominated by linear deformation. Pattern-based interpretation further shows that non-stable deformation is associated with Quaternary unconsolidated sediments, paddy soils, fine-grained soil textures, and urban expansion areas. These results indicate that InSAR-derived kinematic patterns provide an effective interpretive layer for linking railway-corridor displacement, temporal evolution, and environmental context.

title: Relaxing the clear-sky assumption: Cloud-tolerant spatiotemporal fusion via mask-guided feature modulation and temporal-memory collaboration
venue: International Journal of Applied Earth Observation and Geoinformation
abstract: The precise characterization of dynamic Earth surface processes relies on time-series remote sensing imagery with both high spatial fidelity and frequent temporal coverage. While spatiotemporal fusion (STF) bridges this resolution trade-off by integrating complementary observations, its practical application remains constrained by the idealized ”clear-sky assumption”. This requirement often favors the selection of temporally distant cloud-free acquisitions over temporally closer but cloud-contaminated observations, potentially reducing the relevance of reference information. To address this limitation, we propose CloudSTF, a robust framework designed to achieve high-fidelity reconstruction by effectively exploiting partially occluded observations. Our approach employs a Mask-guided Multi-scale Swin Transformer (M 2 ST) encoder to capture cloud spatial patterns and suppress noise propagation during feature extraction. This is coupled with a Cross-temporal Memory-guided Fusion (CTMF) module that adaptively integrates temporal trends with textural details retrieved from a spatio-temporal memory bank. To validate this paradigm, we introduce the Global Cloud-shrouded Regions (GCR-STF) benchmark, a geographically distributed dataset comprising 24 representative agricultural and urban sites across six continents. Extensive experiments demonstrate that CloudSTF consistently outperforms state-of-the-art methods. Additional assessments across varying cloud densities and diverse landscapes further demonstrate the robustness and applicability of CloudSTF under realistic cloud-contaminated conditions. These results suggest that CloudSTF provides a reliable solution for continuous Earth monitoring in realistic, cloud-prone environments. Source code and the GCR-STF benchmark are available at https://github.com/Sichen-Lu/CloudSTF .

title: SFD-Mamba2Net: Structure-Guided Frequency-Enhanced Dual-Stream Mamba2 Network for Coronary Artery Segmentation
abstract: Coronary artery disease (CAD), primarily caused by arterial stenosis or occlusion, remains a leading cause of mortality worldwide. Invasive coronary angiography (ICA) is the clinical gold standard for CAD diagnosis and treatment planning, yet its effectiveness critically depends on accurate coronary artery segmentation and stenosis assessment. However, ICA images are often affected by low contrast, severe noise, and complex multi-scale vascular morphology, substantially challenges existing segmentation methods. This study aims to improve the robustness and reliability of ICA-based coronary artery segmentation and stenosis detection by learning structure-consistent representations that jointly capture geometric priors, cross-dataset variability, long-range spatial dependencies, and frequency-aware vascular features. We propose SFD-Mamba2Net , an end-to-end framework for coronary artery segmentation and stenosis detection. A Curvature-Aware Structural Enhancement (CASE) module is introduced in the encoder to highlight elongated vascular structures while suppressing background interference. To alleviate performance degradation induced by inter-dataset discrepancies, a Supervised Domain Adaptation (SDA) strategy is incorporated at the bottleneck to encourage domain-invariant feature learning. Long-range spatial dependencies and complex vessel topology are modeled via an Axial-Alternating Dual-Stream Mamba2 (AA-DS Mamba2) module. In the decoder, a Progressive High-Frequency Perception (PHFP) module integrates multi-level wavelet decomposition with deep convolution to refine high-frequency vascular details while preserving global structural. Experiments on three large-scale ICA datasets show that SFD-Mamba2Net achieves superior segmentation accuracy and strong cross-domain generalization, obtaining Dice scores of 89.31%, 77.01%, and 74.14% on JSPH-ICA, DCA1, and ARCADE, respectively. It also achieves high true positive and positive predictive values in stenosis detection, demonstrating robustness and clinical potential.

title: SpikeHSA: Heterogeneous Space-Aligned Spiking Hashing for cross-modal retrieval
abstract: Spiking Neural Networks (SNNs) offer a promising paradigm for cross-modal hashing (CMH) due to their biological plausibility and energy efficiency. However, sparse spike-driven representations can limit semantic encoding, while conventional single-space alignment is insufficient to capture complementary fine-grained cross-modal semantics. To address these issues, we propose SpikeHSA, a Heterogeneous Space-Aligned Spiking Hashing framework for Cross-Modal Retrieval. Inspired by neuronal threshold diversity, SpikeHSA introduces the Heterogeneous Leaky Integrate-and-Fire (H-LIF) neuron, which assigns dimension-specific thresholds to diversify spiking responses and improve the information density of spike-based representations. We further develop a Heterogeneous Space Alignment (HSA) strategy that projects image, text, and fused multimodal representations into multiple heterogeneous spaces and aligns each unimodal representation with the fused semantic reference. Extensive experiments on three widely used benchmarks demonstrate that, with convolutional image encoders, SpikeHSA improves mAP by up to 4.6% over ANN-based baselines and 4.3% over the SNN-based method, while requiring as little as approximately one-eighth of the estimated inference energy of non-spiking baselines Code will be available at https://github.com/whisper233/SpikeHSA .

title: Efficient optimal scale combination selection via granular sequential three-way decision
abstract: Optimal scale combination (OSC) selection is crucial for knowledge extraction in multi-scale decision systems (MDSs). However, existing multi-scale rough set models typically represent the three regions as unions of equivalence classes, losing the structural information of equivalence classes and hindering rule extraction. Moreover, most OSC selection algorithms adopt a fine-to-coarse backward search strategy, which not only contradicts the human coarse-to-fine cognitive mode but also is inefficient on large-scale datasets due to scale combination explosion. To address these issues, a granular sequential three-way decision model for MDSs (GrS3WD-M) is developed, and then an efficient forward optimal scale combination selection algorithm (FOSC) is designed. First, a two-step trisecting strategy is proposed to accelerate boundary region reduction, and then GrS3WD-M based on granular rough sets is developed to preserve the structural information of equivalence classes. As a result, rules can be directly extracted from equivalence classes in the positive region, while redundant computation during granulation is avoided. Second, the core scale combination is defined, an equivalent computational formula is derived, and an efficient algorithm based on GrS3WD-M and attribute grouping is proposed for its computation. Finally, the outer significance of attributes in MDSs is defined, and an efficient method for computing it is presented. Furthermore, the FOSC algorithm is proposed, which starts from the core scale combination and uses the outer significance as a heuristic to guide a coarse-to-fine forward search. Experimental results show that, compared with the state-of-the-art OSC selection algorithms, FOSC improves the average computational efficiency by more than 50 times.

title: Adaptive background suppression-based plume identification, emission estimation, and ground validation of coal mine methane in Changzhi, Shanxi, China
venue: International Journal of Applied Earth Observation and Geoinformation
abstract: This study developed a coal mine methane remote-sensing monitoring framework centered on adaptive background suppression using high-spatial-resolution multispectral data from Sentinel-2. The framework integrates methane column enhancement retrieval, automated plume detection, and emission flux estimation. Specifically, bilateral filtering and the multi-band single-pass (MBSP) method were used to retrieve methane column enhancements; a methane plume detection algorithm combining NDVI-based stratification, adaptive segmentation, morphological processing, and wind-field constraints was developed; and coal mine methane emission fluxes were quantified using the integrated mass enhancement (IME) method. Application to a pilot coal enterprise in Changzhi during 2024 demonstrated that the proposed framework effectively reduced weak vegetation-background effects and heterogeneous high-intensity interference while preserving plume topological consistency. Sentinel-2 also provided an observation frequency more than eight times higher than that of EMIT. The mean satellite-derived emission rate for the pilot enterprise was 1023.57 ± 266.84 kg ⋅ h − 1 , with a mean relative deviation of 14.47% from ground-based measurements. The relatively large deviations and daily-scale fluctuations observed during some periods were mainly attributed to uncertainties associated with the spectral resolution of Sentinel-2, surface heterogeneity, algorithm parameter settings, and ERA5 wind-field data. A comparison with the EDGAR inventory revealed broad consistency in regional spatial emission patterns. However, the higher-resolution Sentinel-2 data detected potential coal-related emission signals in several grid cells absent from EDGAR, accounting for 22.2% of the potential emission grids identified in Changzhi. On a regional scale, EDGAR’s annual emission estimate for Changzhi was 32.11% higher than the Sentinel-2 annualized estimate derived in this study.

Leveraging unlabeled data via semi-supervised contrastive learning for enhanced monocular depth estimation
abstract: Accurate monocular depth estimation with limited annotations remains a critical challenge in real-world scenarios. Existing supervised approaches heavily rely on large-scale dense annotations, the acquisition of which is costly and difficult to scale, while self-supervised methods often depend on restrictive geometric assumptions and additional information such as camera parameters or multi-view consistency, thereby limiting their generalization under sparse or noisy supervision. To bridge this gap, we propose TriConDepth, a novel semi-supervised framework that leverages contrastive learning (CL) to explore both labeled and unlabeled data effectively. The method comprises three stages: unsupervised image-level CL to extract global geometry-invariant structures from unlabeled images, empowering the embedding space with global contextual awareness; supervised pixel-level CL performed on labeled images to enhance local depth-aware feature discriminability; and a consistency-based semi-supervised strategy to align intermediate embeddings and ensure robust predictions under perturbations. To address incomplete annotations within labeled data, we design a window-based contrastive loss that fully exploits sparse and invalid depth regions. Extensive experiments across varying label ratios on the KITTI and NYU datasets demonstrate that TriConDepth consistently surpasses state-of-the-art alternatives, achieving significant improvements and showcasing the model’s robustness and effectiveness in real-world depth estimation. Code is available at https://github.com/Ketin12138/TriConDepth .

title: Detecting diurnal dynamics of cotton leaf inclination angle under water-salt stress
abstract: Leaf inclination angle (LIA) dynamics act as a rapid response mechanism to abiotic stress, regulating canopy energy balance and water use efficiency. While the adaptive value of diurnal LIA plasticity (e.g., paraheliotropism) is well-recognized in ecology, most current remote sensing algorithms and ecosystem models still treat canopy architecture as static and neglect stress-induced geometric adjustments. Furthermore, the diurnal dynamics of LIA under combined abiotic stresses, such as concurrent water deficit and salinity, still remain poorly understood. Recent advances in unmanned aerial vehicle (UAV) photogrammetry offer a promising approach for capturing LIA dynamics at high spatial and temporal resolution. However, accurately resolving fine scale, dynamic leaf movements in real environments using UAVs remains challenging. To address these gaps, we developed the Constraint-Assisted Point cloud fusion for Leaf scale Analysis (CAPLA), an integrated UAV analytical workflow that combines deep learning with Structure from Motion (SfM). CAPLA employs 2D semantic masks to strictly constrain 3D mesh reconstruction, effectively mitigating motion-induced artifacts. Independent validation against 19 plot level mean leaf angle (MLA) observations collected at 9:30 am and 12:00 pm yielded an R 2 of 0.89 and an RMSE of 0.9°, supporting plot level MLA estimation under the validated acquisition conditions. CAPLA was subsequently applied across five observation times to characterize diurnal canopy structural dynamics. Importantly, repeated measures analysis of the high frequency observations revealed significant effects of irrigation, salinity, and observation time on MLA, together with a significant irrigation × time interaction ( P = 0.0109), indicating that diurnal MLA trajectories differed among irrigation levels. In contrast, neither the irrigation × salinity interaction ( P = 0.8800) nor the irrigation × salinity × time interaction ( P = 0.9086) was significant. Descriptive differences in within-day variability were nevertheless observed among individual treatment combinations, highlighting the value of time-resolved structural monitoring for characterizing canopy responses to combined water and salinity stresses. These findings highlight the complex structural plasticity of canopies under interacting stresses, emphasizing the critical need to transition from static canopy assumptions to dynamic structural monitoring for improving ecosystem models and precision agriculture.

title: Diurnal coupling of total column nitrogen dioxide and aerosol optical depth: Insights from the Pandora Asia network
abstract: To improve understanding of air quality in Asia and support satellite validation, the Korean government launched the Pandora Asia Network (PAN) in 2021. The high temporal resolution and simultaneous retrievals of nitrogen dioxide (NO 2 ) and aerosol optical depth (AOD) from the PAN allow for detailed analysis of aerosol and precursor variability. This study evaluated NO 2 and AOD levels at various sites across major Asian cities with different air quality regulations, using consistent quality measurements from Pandora and satellite data. Generally, AOD from the Visible Infrared Imaging Radiometer Suite (VIIRS) Deep Blue product showed good agreement with the PAN retrievals, whereas TROPOspheric Monitoring Instrument (TROPOMI) generally underestimated NO 2 levels relative to Pandora, especially in highly polluted cities such as Dhaka and Singapore. The NO 2 -to-AOD ratio (NAR), which assesses aerosol characteristics associated with NO 2 sources, was higher in major cities such as Seoul and Singapore, whereas lower values were observed in areas with uncontrolled or limited combustion activity. Differences in NO 2 measurements between TROPOMI and Pandora led to discrepancies in NAR between satellite and ground-based data, particularly in Singapore, Islamabad, and Dhaka. Using high-frequency PAN sampling, we calculated the daily correlation coefficient between AOD and NO 2 (r d ) at each site. High values of r d were observed in Islamabad and Dhaka, where ammonia (NH 3 ) and NO 2 levels were elevated; both are important tracers of nitrate aerosol formation. This study estimated the NO x emission contribution factor to AOD (NCF) based on a statistical relationship among r d , NO 2 , NH 3 , and water vapor (H 2 O), which can serve as a diagnostic tool for evaluating aerosol emission sources across Asian countries.

title: An Adaptive Dynamic AI-driven ParameTerization (ADAPT) framework for global hourly gross primary productivity estimation
venue: ISPRS Journal of Photogrammetry and Remote Sensing
abstract: High-frequency estimation of gross primary productivity (GPP) is crucial for understanding terrestrial carbon dynamics and ecosystem responses to rapidly changing environmental conditions. However, accurate GPP estimation at short-term timescales remains challenging, as it requires accounting for both instantaneous physiological reactions and legacy effects from antecedent environments. While light response curve (LRC) models effectively represent diurnal photosynthetic variations by capturing nonlinear light saturation, their global application has been constrained by static parameterizations. To address this, we propose the Adaptive Dynamic AI-driven ParameTerization (ADAPT) framework, which couples an LRC model with a deep learning approach. By integrating satellite-derived vegetation indices and 15-day antecedent meteorological statistics, ADAPT dynamically retrieves daily physiological parameters, enabling spatially explicit and temporally dynamic LRC parameterization. Using 328 eddy covariance flux sites globally (2001–2024), the dynamically parameterized model (LRC-DP) substantially mitigated underestimation biases associated with static models, achieving a site-level root mean squared error (RMSE) of 343.7 g C m −2 yr −1 for annual GPP. Against existing hourly products, ADAPT reduced RMSE by 25.8–32.4%, successfully reproducing midday peak productivity by overcoming the limitations of linear light-use efficiency assumptions and purely data-driven approaches. Global application at 0.05° resolution demonstrated that ADAPT captures sub-daily photosynthetic sensitivities and interannual variability consistent with global products. Highlighting its robustness under extreme climate stress, ADAPT demonstrated enhanced capability over existing products by accurately capturing daily and sub-daily GPP declines during heatwaves in the United States and Australia. This study highlights that integrating physiological mechanisms with dynamic parameterizations effectively resolves traditional scaling bottlenecks, advancing our capability to monitor high-resolution land–atmosphere carbon exchanges under climate extremes.

title: Spectral unmixing of hyperspectral lidar signals considering laser beam profile
venue: ISPRS Journal of Photogrammetry and Remote Sensing
abstract: Full-waveform hyperspectral LiDAR (FWHSL) provides range-resolved spectral measurements and enables quantitative interpretation of multiple targets within a laser footprint. Conventional spectral unmixing (SU), originally developed for passive hyperspectral imagery, estimates the fractional contribution of each endmember from a mixed spectrum and commonly relates this abundance to the area proportion of the corresponding target within pixels. However, HSL is an active sensing modality, and its measured mixed spectrum is inherently modulated by the spatial energy distribution of the emitted laser beam. As a result, in HSL data, the spectral contribution of a target depends not only on its reflectance and geometric coverage, but also on its position within the beam footprint. Directly applying conventional SU to HSL therefore ignores this intrinsic beam-profile weighting and can lead to a mismatch between energy-weighted spectral abundance and true geometric area proportion. To address this problem, this study formulates the beam-profile-induced energy-to-area mismatch and proposes a beam-profile-constrained geometric spectral unmixing method for FWHSL data. The method interprets the mixed spectrum as an energy constraint and uses a known, calibrated Gaussian beam profile together with a low-dimensional circular-arc boundary model to retrieve target area proportions. Simulations with controlled binary mixtures show that the method outperforms a linear mixing model (LMM)-only baseline, reducing mean relative error (RE) from 21.55 % to 9.64 % and composite root mean square error (CRMSE) from 25.81 % to 13.43 %. A laboratory 101-channel FWHSL system experiment further validates the method using leaf-wood board, leaf-red brick, and leaf-ceramic tile binary mixtures and image-based ground truth. Relative to the direct LMM baseline, the proposed method reduces the overall mean absolute error (MAE) from 0.2061 to 0.1321, across-group root mean square error (ARMSE) from 0.1412 to 0.0843, mean RE from 24.15 % to 15.48 %, and mean CRMSE from 0.1158 to 0.0660. These changes correspond to reductions of 35.90 %, 40.27 %, 35.91 %, and 42.97 %, respectively. These results indicate that accounting for laser beam-profile weighting can improve geometric area-proportion retrieval in FWHSL SU, particularly when the target boundary intersects beam-sensitive regions with large spatial energy gradients. The current validation is limited to binary mixtures with locally smooth boundaries and a known or calibrated beam profile. Extension to unknown or irregular beam profiles, multi-material mixtures, and more complex intra-footprint geometries remain a subject for future research.

title: Biophysical effects of afforestation on local land surface temperature in china: A comprehensive analysis incorporating forest age and afforestation intensity
venue: International Journal of Applied Earth Observation and Geoinformation
abstract: Afforestation changes the surface biogeochemical and biophysical processes and thus affects land surface temperature (LST). The historic studies on the LST effect of afforestation ignored the variation of energy exchange caused by the difference in forest structure such as LAI, vegetation fraction, and canopy height that is directly related to forest age. In this study, we constructed a model of the Land Surface Temperature Effect from Afforestation (LSTEA) considering forest age and afforestation intensity for different climate zones in China and then analyzed the biophysical effects on LST from historical and future afforestation in China. Results showed that (1) the LSTEA model revealed significant spatial and seasonal variability, with minimal warming effects in winter and pronounced cooling effects in other seasons. (2) from 1990 to 2020, the total national afforestation area reached 71.44 × 10 4 km 2 , of which 78.2 % originated from cropland and 12 % from grassland. The current afforestation has induced a grid-/national cooling effect of −0.35 ℃/-0.29 ℃ in summer and −0.26 ℃/-0.21 ℃ in winter by 2021. (3) The projected afforestation initiatives are projected to induce progressively intensifying cooling effects during 2030–2100. By 2100, it will bring a summer grid-/national cooling effect of −1.29 ℃/-0.51 ℃, −0.90 ℃/-0.35 ℃ and −0.75 ℃/-0.28 ℃ under the SSP-RCP2.6, SSP2-RCP4.5 and SSP5-RCP8.5 scenario respectively. The projected years of 2060 in SSP1-RCP2.6, 2070 in SSP-RCP4.5, and SSP-RCP8.5 will be the time that the maximum of LST effects in the near decades. Our study highlights the important role of afforestation as a mitigation strategy for climate change.

title: A two-stage transformer framework for reconstructing hourly 1 km all-weather land surface temperature using cross-scale transfer learning
venue: International Journal of Applied Earth Observation and Geoinformation
abstract: High spatiotemporal resolution land surface temperature (LST) reconstruction is essential for analyzing land-atmosphere interactions and thermal environmental dynamics. Thermal infrared observations, the primary source of regional and global LST, are affected by cloud contamination, scale discrepancies, and distribution shifts. Meanwhile, reconstruction methods struggle to provide both hourly continuity and kilometer-scale detail, and cross-scale fusion often causes spatial over-smoothing. To address these limitations, we propose ST-LSTrans, a two-stage Transformer framework for reconstructing regional hourly 1 km all-weather LST. It uses cross-scale transfer learning with global pre-training on hourly ∼6.25 km CLDAS LST to capture regional thermodynamic evolution and local fine-tuning on four-times-daily 1000 m MODIS LST to recover kilometer-scale thermal heterogeneity. A KL divergence constraint is introduced to reduce distribution shifts and spatial over-smoothing during cross-scale fusion. Validation results based on multi-source datasets show that the global pre-training stage achieved an average RMSE of 1.13 K, while the local fine-tuning stage achieved an average RMSE of 1.06 K, with the minimum RMSE reaching 0.87 K. Independent Landsat validation showed that the reconstructed product achieved a scene-averaged RMSE of 2.98 K and improved upon the original CLDAS background field. Additional evaluations against VIIRS VNP21, which is generated using an independent temperature-emissivity separation algorithm, confirmed the cross-sensor consistency of the reconstructed LST. Ground-based observations further demonstrated that ST-LSTrans preserved realistic diurnal temperature cycle characteristics under both clear-sky and persistent cloudy conditions. SHAP analysis further revealed scale-dependent transitions in LST driving mechanisms from coarse-scale atmospheric forcing to kilometer-scale terrain and land surface controls. This study provides a unified and interpretable modelling framework for high spatiotemporal resolution LST reconstruction and driving mechanism analysis.

title: AdaGeo-SR: Geo-semantic-guided super-resolution of sentinel-2 imagery with AlphaEarth foundation priors
venue: International Journal of Applied Earth Observation and Geoinformation
abstract: Remote sensing image super-resolution is an important approach for enhancing the spatial detail of Earth observation data. In super-resolving Sentinel-2 multispectral imagery from 10 m to 2.5 m, conventional single-image super-resolution (SISR) methods are largely constrained by purely pixel-driven mechanisms. As a result, they often produce structural discontinuities, blurred edges, and chromatic artifacts when reconstructing complex human-made objects such as narrow roads and farmland boundaries during cross-scale detail reconstruction. To address these limitations, this study proposes a geo-semantic-guided remote sensing super-resolution framework, termed AdaGeo-SR. The framework incorporates dense spatial feature maps extracted from AlphaEarth Foundation (AEF) as geo-semantic priors, providing additional geo-semantic and topological cues for the reconstruction process. To better leverage high-level semantic features, we further design a degradation-simulation-based feature balancing mechanism. By introducing specific degradation conditions during training, this mechanism encourages the network to reduce its over-reliance on the original pixel cues, thereby enhancing its use of external geo-semantic priors. Experiments on the OpenSR-Test and WorldStrat benchmarks show that AdaGeo-SR effectively suppresses structural distortions and hallucination artifacts while maintaining reasonable spectral consistency, leading to improved local geometric coherence. In addition, downstream road extraction experiments using SAM_Road on the NAIP test set further demonstrate that the super-resolved images produced by the proposed framework help reduce mask fragmentation and topological discontinuities. These results highlight the potential of the proposed framework for downstream structure-sensitive tasks and support the generation of structurally more reliable 2.5 m imagery for practical remote sensing applications.

title: A spatiotemporal reconstruction framework for GRACE/GRACE-FO-derived groundwater storage anomalies based on historical phase-constrained gap filling and physics-guided global–local downscaling
venue: International Journal of Applied Earth Observation and Geoinformation
abstract: Observations from the Gravity Recovery and Climate Experiment (GRACE) and GRACE Follow-On (GRACE-FO) provide essential information on terrestrial water storage anomalies (TWSA), from which groundwater storage anomalies (GWSA) can be derived. However, the approximately 11-month mission gap and the coarse spatial resolution of the original products constrain their application in regional groundwater monitoring and water-resource assessment. This study developed an integrated spatiotemporal reconstruction framework for the Three-North Region of China by combining historical phase-constrained gap filling with physics-guided global–local downscaling. First, a Kling-Gupta Efficiency-based singular spectrum analysis method (KGC-SSA) was developed to reconstruct the mission gap without external forcing data. Second, a physics-guided global–local-residual geographically weighted extreme gradient boosting framework (GLR-GWXGB) was developed to downscale GWSA to 1 km under grid-wise coarse-scale consistency constraints. KGC-SSA yielded a mean ensemble reconstruction spread of 0.06 cm during the mission gap and performed broadly comparably to benchmark methods. Relative to the global benchmark model, GLR-GWXGB improved internal validation performance, preserved regional-scale consistency with the original GRACE-derived GWSA, and enhanced local spatial detail. Correlations with groundwater observations improved at more than 70% of monitoring sites. The reconstructed 1 km product further captured persistent groundwater-storage decline during 2002–2022, with intensified depletion after approximately 2012, while retaining the dominant long-term and seasonal characteristics of the original series. These results demonstrate that the proposed framework provides a robust approach for generating temporally continuous and spatially refined groundwater-storage information from GRACE/GRACE-FO observations.

Class-Balanced Softmax: A Bayes theory-based method for long-tailed recognition
abstract: Models trained on long-tailed data using standard softmax tend to exhibit higher training error and a larger generalisation gap for classes with fewer training samples. We characterise this class-wise disparity as the preference issue and quantify it using a new metric, the model imbalance level $I$. To understand this issue, we analyse how imbalanced training data adversely affects class-wise gradients under standard softmax training. This paper then develops a finite-data Generalised Balanced Softmax (GBS) framework for analysing and mitigating the preference issue. The framework uses the training-time logit adjustment $z_{nc}+β\log|N_c|$, which is algebraically identical to the training-time logit-adjusted loss of Menon et al. (2021) when $τ=β$. The case $β=1$ also coincides with Balanced Softmax and with the unit adjustment supported by the Fisher-consistency argument under the true data distribution, corresponding to an idealised infinite-data setting. Building on this existing loss family, this paper uses a heuristic power-law assumption to motivate the adjustable coefficient and studies how $β$ affects trained models. Across the evaluated long-tailed benchmarks, $β=1$ does not attain the highest average testing recall on most datasets, showing that a different coefficient can be preferable when training on finite data. The selected values of $β$ reduce $I$ and improve average testing recall relative to the $β=1$ reference, while retaining negligible computational overhead and compatibility with existing representation-learning frameworks.

Enhancing learning efficiency in spiking neural networks via expanded representation and neuronal heterogeneity
abstract: Spiking Neural Networks (SNNs) remain limited by three coupled deficiencies in existing neuron models: binary spikes collapse continuous membrane states into 0/1 events, causing severe quantization loss; fixed or homogeneous thresholds cannot adapt to instantaneous inputs and neuron-wise dynamics; and conventional hard/soft reset rules either discard useful residual membrane information or retain excessive residual potential, leading to redundant firing. To address these limitations, we propose the dynamic threshold feedback reset leaky integrate-and-multi-valued-fire (DTFR-LIMF) neuron. Multi-valued firing expands spike states to mitigate spatial-domain entropy loss, an input-dependent dynamic threshold regulates firing difficulty at the neuron level, and a feedback reset mechanism applies history-dependent reward-penalty adjustment to improve temporal dynamics and suppress redundant spikes. For stable optimization of multi-valued firing, we further design a threshold-dependent surrogate gradient (TdSG) and an accelerated variant ( T 2 TdSG). To preserve event-driven efficiency during inference, we introduce an integer-to-binary (I2B) conversion scheme and binary-based energy metrics. Experiments on static and neuromorphic benchmarks show state-of-the-art performance, achieving 82.8% on CIFAR100, 69.89% on Tiny-ImageNet, and 89.4% on CIFAR10-DVS, while I2B reduces synaptic operations by 21%–36%.

Frequency-domain Guided Attention-Differential Enhancement Network for medical image segmentation
abstract: Medical image segmentation remains a critical yet challenging task in pattern recognition, as extracting discriminative features is often hindered by complex anatomical structures with indistinct boundaries, low contrast, overlapping tissues, and inherent imaging noise. Consequently, these characteristics disrupt stable pattern representations, making segmentation approaches sensitive to intensity variations and anatomical ambiguities. To address these issues, we propose a Frequency-domain Guided Attention-Differential Enhancement Network (FDANet) for medical image segmentation. Our FDANet explicitly exploits frequency-domain representations, where low-frequency components preserve global anatomical layouts and high-frequency components emphasize structural details, while rich semantic information is simultaneously mined from the spatial domain. Additionally, to mitigate distribution discrepancies between the spatial and frequency domains while suppressing noise introduced during the fusion process, we design a Frequency-domain Differential Fusion Module (FDFM). Specifically, we first obtain two sets of feature embeddings in the frequency domain and spatial domain respectively, and utilize 2D Rotary Position Embedding (RoPE) to embed 2D relative spatial position information into these vectors to generate position-aware feature representations. Then we perform two independent self-attention operations within the spatial and frequency domains respectively, concatenate the resulting attention weights, and apply a learnable differential mechanism to adaptively attenuate redundant and noisy activations, thereby enabling more reliable exploitation of complementary cues. Finally, Semantic Consistency Loss (SCL) is employed to enforce semantic alignment between the fused frequency-domain and spatial-domain features, further enhancing the coherence of representations. We conduct extensive experiments on the CXRS, ISIC17, ISIC18, VinDr-RibCXR, and FracAtlas datasets. Experimental results and visualizations show that our method achieves competitive performance across all five benchmarks, consistently outperforming recent Transformer and Mamba-based baselines on most metrics under the same training protocol, while remaining on par with the strongest SAM-based models, illustrating its effectiveness. The code is publicly available at https://github.com/libaitian02/FDANet .

MEFCL: Reliability-aware multi-view edge-filtered contrastive learning for graph recommendation
abstract: Multi-view learning has become an important paradigm for recommender systems by leveraging complementary collaborative semantics from heterogeneous structural perspectives. Existing graph contrastive recommendation methods, however, predominantly rely on random perturbations or heuristic view construction, which may introduce unreliable semantic consistency and noisy collaborative signals. To address these challenges, we propose MEFCL, a reliability-aware multi-view edge-filtered contrastive learning framework for graph recommendation. Specifically, MEFCL formulates recommendation as a multi-view collaborative representation learning problem and constructs complementary local structural and global collaborative views to capture fine-grained neighborhood semantics and high-order structural relationships, respectively. To improve the reliability of multi-view representations, we further develop an edge-level reliability fusion mechanism that jointly evaluates global structural importance and local structural consistency using PageRank centrality and Weisfeiler–Lehman graph kernels. Based on the fused reliability signals, unreliable interactions are filtered before global collaborative modeling to generate noise-resilient contrastive views. In addition, a cross-view contrastive alignment objective is introduced to enhance representation consistency and robustness across different structural views. Extensive experiments on multiple real-world recommendation benchmarks demonstrate that MEFCL consistently outperforms state-of-the-art methods in terms of recommendation accuracy and robustness, particularly under noisy interaction settings and long-tail recommendation scenarios.
